title: Ekantik dharma: four together
hook: a scripture made of questions asked out loud in a village courtyard, and a love for God that needs three companions
carry: ekantik dharma: dharma, self-knowledge, detachment and bhakti together
tomorrow: A letter that begins with no harm

segments.voice: Yesterday, Nilkanth became Sahajanand, and his mantra became a greeting. Jay Swaminarayan: every hello remembers God.

Evening in a village in Gujarat. A courtyard, a raised seat, a crowd on the ground: farmers, merchants, robed sadhus, children at the edges. The teacher on the seat is Swaminarayan, and he invites questions. Someone asks a hard one. Why does the mind keep running back to the same old cravings, even after years of devotion? He answers. Someone pushes back. He answers again. And off to one side, a few senior sadhus listen very closely, because they're going to write this down. Today, a holy book that began as a conversation.
screen: `A COURTYARD AT EVENING.` → `SOMEONE ASKS A HARD ONE.` → `SOMEONE WRITES IT DOWN.`

segments.voice: The book is the Vachanamrut. Followers hear the title as vachan, words, and amrut, the nectar of immortality: nectar in the form of words. They hold it as scripture, his own teaching, gathered from talks in Gadhada and other villages, each headed with the place, the setting, even what he was wearing that evening. First, its shape. It arrives as dialogue. A devotee asks, Swaminarayan answers, and sometimes he turns it around and asks the room. Then, the questions. How do you know if your devotion is real? What do you do with anger toward someone in your own community? Why does a person who has heard good teaching still not change? Kitchen-table questions, treated as worth a scripture. Last, the answer at its heart, which the tradition calls ekantik dharma: a whole-hearted life held up by four things together. Dharma, doing what's right. Knowing the self, the atman, as distinct from the body. Vairagya, detachment. And bhakti, love for God. Many teachers in the tradition read the four this way: love for God without right conduct goes hollow; detachment without love goes dry; knowing the self without devotion can turn proud. Picture the legs of a cot. Take one away and the whole thing tips. So when someone in the courtyard asks why old cravings keep coming back after years of devotion, the answer, read this way, isn't only pray harder. It's look at all four.
screen: `VACHANAMRUT — NECTAR IN WORDS` · `A SCRIPTURE THAT BEGINS AS DIALOGUE` · `EKANTIK DHARMA` · `DHARMA · THE SELF · DETACHMENT · BHAKTI` · `ALL FOUR, TOGETHER`

segments.voice: Give one breath to each leg of the cot: doing what's right, knowing yourself as more than the body, letting go, and love, for one face or, if you pray, for God. Then notice, without judging, which leg feels steady today and which one wobbles, and rest on the whole cot for a few breaths.
Gujarat's Swaminarayan. Today, the Vachanamrut, his teaching kept as questions and answers, and its heart: ekantik dharma, four things held together. Today's word.
Your line: ekantik dharma, dharma, self-knowledge, detachment and bhakti together. In his courtyard, love for God never stood alone. See you tomorrow.

chat.meaning: In the Vachanamrut, ekantik dharma holds four together: dharma, knowing the self as more than the body, detachment, and bhakti. Love for God is the heart, and it needs the other three.
